title: FDA requests removal of strongest warning against using cholesterol-lowering statins during pregnancy; still advises most pregnant patients should stop taking statins
journal: US Food and Drug Administration, Drug Safety Communication, 20 July 2021
result: FDA requested removal of the contraindication of all statins in pregnancy, present since the first approval in 1987, while advising that most patients stop statins when pregnancy is recognised and that breastfeeding is not recommended during statin treatment. Observational studies controlled for diabetes did not identify a drug-associated risk of major birth defects: in a 2015 Medicaid cohort of 1152 exposed pregnancies against 886,996 controls, the relative risk of congenital malformations after first-trimester exposure was 1.07 (95% CI 0.85 to 1.37). Data are insufficient to determine miscarriage risk: in a cohort of 281 exposed and 2643 control pregnancies (McGrogan et al. 2017) miscarriage occurred in 25% against 21%, adjusted HR 1.64 (1.1 to 2.46), with possible residual confounding by diabetes type and severity. Because statins decrease the synthesis of cholesterol and possibly other substances, they could harm an unborn baby.
